thread.title: Will the Bear Win Out? What to Watch This Week - TheStreet

author: Katherine Ross
title: Will the Bear Win Out? What to Watch This Week - TheStreet
text:
It's been a tough couple of weeks in the market.
TheStreet's London Bureau chief, Martin Baccardax talked about the market's volatility with Katherine Ross.
Earnings Season It's no surprise that earnings season is upon us. On Thursday, Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet ( SNAP ) shocked Wall Street by beating on bottom lines, but disappointing when it came to the top lines.
When TheStreet recorded the podcast on Friday, Oct. 26, the markets were still reeling from the tech darlings failing to deliver.
The big reporters on Thursday night were Amazon, Alphabet, Intel ( INTC ) and Snap ( SNAP ) .
Jim Cramer on How New Investors Handle This Market Snap shed more daily active users, causing the stock to sink even as the company beat earnings per share estimates.
Baccardax believes that Snap's decline may be in the favor of Facebook. The reason, for anyone not fluent in social media, is due to Instagram stories. Facebook reports on Tuesday, Oct. 30.
Another company that may be a market mover is Apple ( AAPL ) , which will report on Thursday, Nov. 1. The company will wrap up the FANG earnings.
Does the Market Even Care About Earnings Anymore? TheStreet has offered a couple of different viewpoints. TheStreet's Jacob Sonenshine takes a look at the trends, Kenny Polcari, director of O'Neil Securities at the New York Stock Exchange, argued that it does.
Does Earnings Season Matter? NYSE Trader Breaks Down the Market and More So, it's only fair to get another opinion. Baccardax takes a crack at the ultimate question: Do earnings really matter when the market's this volatile?
Hey, New Investors -- Stay Strong Baccardax breaks down what newer or younger investors should do in a volatile market.
Surprisingly, it wasn't 'keep calm and carry on.'
Here's a tidbit: it does have to do with patience and not overexerting yourself in the market.
Earnings Up, Market Down: Keys to your Trading Day Are We in for a Bear Market? Beginning of 2019: Bull or bear?
Baccardax answered that he's leaning more towards the bear, but doesn't think that we'll necessarily enter a bear market.
